name: Starship Flight 15
status: Complete · Ship 42 caught at the Pad 2 tower · booster lost offshore
outcome: Launch success. Ship 42 caught by the Pad 2 tower chopsticks at about 3:20 p.m. CST on Nov 14, the first Starship upper-stage catch. Booster B22 was lost offshore: boostback ended early on a low-fuel-mass alarm, and the flight termination system fired after the landing burn.
catchNote: Flight 15 is complete. Ship 42 was caught by the Pad 2 tower chopsticks at about 3:20 PM CST on Sat Nov 14, after 14 orbits. The first Starship upper-stage catch. Booster B22 was lost: boostback ended early on a low-fuel-mass alarm, it diverted offshore, and it was destroyed just above the water in the Gulf about 6.5 min after liftoff. The root cause is under investigation. Pad 1 is under reconstruction.

events.label: GO for propellant load
events.see: Flight director poll. Venting usually starts soon after: white vapour clouds around the stack.

events.label: Booster LOX load underway
events.see: Frost and vapour spread over the booster as it fills with super-cold propellant.

events.label: Ship fuel load underway
events.see: Both stages are now loading. Venting from the ship too.

events.label: Raptor engine chill (booster + ship)
events.see: More venting around the engine section at the bottom of the booster.

events.label: Booster propellant load complete
events.see: Earplugs in now.

events.label: Flight director verifies GO for launch
events.see: Last 30 seconds. Eyes on the pad.

events.label: Flame diverter activation
events.see: Water starts flowing through the flame diverter under the mount. You may see spray at the base.

events.label: Booster engine startup
events.see: A bright flash and a billowing cloud at the base. No sound yet.

events.label: LIFTOFF
events.see: The rocket climbs in silence at first. The sound is still on its way to you.

events.label: Liftoff sound arrives
events.see: A deep, crackling roar arrives and keeps rolling for a minute or more. You may feel it in your chest.

events.label: Max Q
events.see: Peak aerodynamic stress. The rocket is climbing out over the Gulf to the east.

events.label: Super Heavy MECO
events.see: Most booster engines shut down. It is now a bright point high in the east.

events.label: Hot staging
events.see: Ship engines light while still attached to the booster. With clear skies you may see a flash and the two stages split. Binoculars help.

events.label: Boostback burn start
events.see: The booster flipped back toward Starbase, then the burn ended early.

events.label: Boostback burn shutdown
events.see: Ended early on a low-fuel-mass alarm. SpaceX says the root cause is still under investigation. Guidance then aborted the tower catch.

events.label: Sonic booms possible (booster return)
events.see: Does not apply. The booster did not return to the tower.

events.label: Booster landing burn at the tower
events.see: Called off. There was no landing burn into the Pad 2 tower.

events.label: BOOSTER LOST
events.see: Tower catch aborted. B22 diverted offshore and was destroyed just above the water in the Gulf about 6.5 min after liftoff, not a clean splashdown. SpaceX: boostback ended early on a low-fuel-mass alarm.

events.label: Landing-burn sound at the tower
events.see: No tower landing-burn roar. The booster was lost offshore.

events.label: Starship engine cutoff
events.see: The ship is far downrange. Follow it on the webcast.

events.label: Orbital insertion burn shutdown
events.see: Ship in orbit at about 275 km, then deploying 26 Starlink V3.

events.label: Payload deploy start
events.see: 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

events.label: Early Hawaii return check
events.see: First chance to bring the ship down early over the ocean.

events.label: Mid Chile return check
events.see: Contingency checkpoint near T+7h15m. The team stayed GO. Ship 42 came home to the tower.

events.label: Final Hawaii return check
events.see: Last contingency checkpoint, near T+20h41m. Teams polled GO for the Pad 2 catch.

events.label: Deorbit burn start
events.see: About T+21:36. The burn flew, and Ship 42 was on the way to the Pad 2 tower.

events.label: Starship entry
events.see: Plasma views on the webcast. SpaceX describes a glide toward Starbase from the Pacific side. The exact ground track is not published here.

events.label: Sonic boom possible (ship return)
events.see: Ship slowed through the speed of sound near Starbase on the way to the catch. Timing was an estimate.

events.label: Starship transonic
events.see: Scan the sky above and around the tower for a falling dot, belly first.

events.label: Ship landing burn start
events.see: Engines light just above the tower.

events.label: Landing flip
events.see: The ship swings from belly-first to upright. This is the big moment to watch.

events.label: SHIP CATCH
events.see: Caught. The Pad 2 tower chopsticks caught Ship 42 at about 3:20 PM CST, after 14 orbits. The first Starship upper-stage catch.

events.label: Ship landing-burn sound arrives
events.see: The roar of the ship landing burn arrived after the catch was visible. The catch is complete, so this is no longer an alert.
